supports: The Trump File page says a 1996 Senate investigations committee recognized that the Semion Mogilevich Organization operated in the United States.

The page lists Robert Maxwell, Jacob Bogatin, David Bogatin, Mikhail Sheferovsky, Vyacheslav Ivankov, Vahtang Ubiriya, and Leib Yermolkin as Mogilevich associates, then asserts that at least two had ties to Donald Trump.
https://trumpfile.org/a-senate-hearing-c.limitations: This is the page’s own account. It does not identify which associates had Trump ties, describe those ties, or provide supporting evidence for that assertion in the entry.

supports: CNN published a May 16, 1996 report about Senate Governmental Affairs Committee testimony concerning Russian organized crime and alleged Russian-Italian Mafia cooperation.
CNN attributes the allegations to witnesses, including Michael Franzese, and reports officials’ testimony about criminal activity.
http://us.cnn.com/US/9605/16/russian.mob.limitations: CNN does not identify Semion Mogilevich or his organization, report a committee finding about that organization, or connect the hearing to Donald Trump. Its mention of hockey player Alexander Mogilny is not evidence about Semion Mogilevich.

supports: The official Senate hearing publication is titled “Russian Organized Crime in the United States” and records a hearing on May 15, 1996.
At printed page 86 (PDF page 92), the hearing publication lists “MOGILEViCH ORGANIZATION” and the name “Semion Mogielvich” (spelling as extracted from the PDF).
https://trumpfile.org/wp-content/uploads.limitations: The list establishes that the organization and name appear in the hearing publication; it does not by itself establish a formal committee finding or any connection to Donald Trump.

focused_rescue.method: Fetched the PDF linked from the supplied Trump File page and extracted its text; checked the title/date and the Mogilevich organization list at printed page 86 (PDF page 92).

blockers: Still missing: a reliable account identifying which Mogilevich associate or associates had a documented tie to Donald Trump, what that tie was, and evidence that connects this hearing to Trump. The Trump File page asserts that at least two associates had Trump ties but does not identify or substantiate them. The official hearing publication lists the Mogilevich Organization, but does not establish a formal Senate finding; any later use of this event should correct “Senate confirms” to wording that says the hearing publication lists the organization.
prior_terminal_history.rationale: One focused source check resolved only the narrow question of whether the Senate hearing publication named the organization: its printed page 86 list does. CNN covers Russian organized crime testimony generally, while the Trump File page supplies an undocumented assertion about unnamed associates’ Trump ties. The evidence does not establish the Trump nexus required to complete this Trump-focused record, so the prior hold remains a hold and no reader-facing copy or impact score is proposed.
